angle: Inside a mirrored crystal sauna — a hard-faceted steel shell wrapped in steam and a heat source — does the acoustic space stay legible enough to move through, or does the geometry collapse into a wash a blind body cannot read; and if it does collapse, is that a defect of the room or the actual point of a sauna, a space designed to be un-navigated?
correction_moment: I went in expecting the titanium facets to shatter the sound into hard slap-echo I could parse, and instead the löyly — the steam burst off the stones — swallowed every reflection into a soft dead close, on my second sit, and the geometry I'd been mapping simply stopped answering.
cross_cite: There is a reading that treats the acoustic collapse as a fault to be engineered out — more absorptive baffling, a fixed audible reference at the door; but recording what the collapse does to a body may matter more than repairing it, because a room designed to unmap you is not obviously a broken room.
opening_scene: A sauna is one of the few rooms built to make you stop reading it.
resisting_example: A regular at a Finnish public sauna told the artists during the Skelleftea build that she comes precisely to lose her bearings — that a sauna where you always know exactly where the door is has failed at the one thing a sauna is for.
